evidence.title: Lowell Township board votes against data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Confirms the proposed six-month data-center moratorium (Ordinance 01-2026R) failed 2-5 at the Township Board's Monday night meeting; only the Clerk and Treasurer voted yes.
evidence.quote: LOWELL TOWNSHIP, Mich. (WOOD) — Lowell Township leaders have declined to pass a six-month moratorium on data centers. The measure failed in a 2-5 vote at Monday night’s meeting of the Lowell Township Board ... Ultimately, however, only Township Clerk Monica Burtt and Treasurer Ronda Benedict voted yes on the moratorium. The five remaining board members voted no.

evidence.title: Residents threaten recall after Lowell Township rejects data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Corroborates the same rejection, with an article publication/update timestamp (May 19) consistent with the 'Monday night' vote falling on May 18, 2026, matching the row's existing date.
evidence.quote: Residents threaten recall after Lowell Township rejects data center moratorium - Updated: May. 19

decisions.notes: REMOVE: independently confirmed via two more news sources (WOOD-TV, MLive) that Lowell Township's proposed data-center moratorium (Ordinance 01-2026R) was never adopted -- it failed 2-5 at the Township Board's meeting on Monday, May 18, 2026 (matching the row's already-stated vote date and count). No moratorium instrument was ever in effect in Lowell Township; the row's current enacted_status of 'expired' is factually wrong for an instrument that was never adopted (nothing existed to expire). The board instead formed a citizen/planning-commission committee to work toward a future ordinance, which is not itself a moratorium. This row should not exist in the moratorium inventory.
